suggestions: Replace the nested Zscore–product–Tanh stack with a single log-ratio spread: Zscore(log(Ma(volume,20)/Ma(volume,60)) - log(Ma((high-low)/close,20)/Ma((high-low)/close,60)), 60). Rationale: the hypothesis is co-movement (participation rising while realized range compresses), not independent extremes; one log-difference enforces that joint pattern with fewer nonlinear layers, eliminates the unstable Inverse(Std) tail that overfits near-zero-volatility names, and removes redundant bounding transforms that amplify idiosyncratic spikes.

Swap Inverse(Std((high-low)/close,20)) for a bounded rank of smoothed range: Rank(Ma(volume,20)/Ma(volume,60)) - Rank(Ma((high-low)/close,20)). Rationale: rank subtraction measures the volume-elevation vs range-compression wedge directly on a 0–1 scale, caps cross-sectional outlier influence, and avoids multiplying unbounded z-scores or inverting variance estimates—both common sources of in-sample fit that fail on validation (rank_ic_valid 0.0041 vs rank_ic 0.0099).

Collapse the interaction to one interpretable ratio and one normalization: Rank(Ma(volume,20) / (Ma((high-low)/close,20) + 1e-6)) or Zscore(Ma(volume,20) / Ma((high-low)/close,20), 60). Rationale: 'high volume per unit of price excursion' is the literal accumulation-under-compression story; a single ratio removes three transformation stages (inner z-scores, multiplicative interaction, Tanh), cuts free parameters/lookbacks from {20,60}×2 to one shared pair, and yields a smoother, more parsimonious signal less prone to tuning specific window combinations on training noise.
